conclusion: Only 11.0% of the training reviews are negative (8.1 positive per negative). Accuracy is misleading; models are compared with F1-macro and PR-AUC of the negative class and trained with class weights.

Negative reviewers had a median of 24.3 h at the time of the review vs 32.8 h for positive reviewers (less playtime); ANOVA eta2 = 0.006, rank-biserial r = -0.107 (small). H1 SUPPORTED (effect small).

Negative share by playtime at review: 40.1% for '<1h', minimum 8.4% for '10-20h', 11.9% for '1000h+'. The relation is U-shaped: players who quit very early and very experienced players are both more negative than mid-range players, so the linear correlation is close to zero although the groups differ strongly.
Negative reviews have a median of 29 words vs 10 for positive (longer); r = +0.325 (medium). H2 SUPPORTED (effect medium). Review length is a useful engineered feature.
Early-access reviews: 13.4% negative vs 10.7% otherwise (V = 0.026); free copies: 10.3% vs 11.0% (V = 0.004). H3 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (significant only for early-access reviews; effect negligible).
The negative share ranges from 1.3% to 37.5% among the 20 largest games; Cramer's V = 0.347 (medium). app_name is kept as a one-hot candidate feature.

Clear sentiment vocabulary separates the classes (negative markers: no, they, money, not, fix, refund; positive markers: fun, great, good, best, amazing, love). Text is expected to be the main predictor (RQ1); negations motivate bigrams in TF-IDF.

9 of 10 numeric features have skewness > 1; Pearson's r with the target changes by up to 0.26 (votes_helpful) between raw and log1p values. The log1p transformation and rank-based statistics are justified.

Among features known at review time the strongest relation with the target is word_count (rho = -0.176, small); numeric features alone are weak predictors, the text has to carry most of the signal. Post-publication columns (votes, comments, later playtime) stay excluded from the model even where they correlate.
The yearly negative share varies between 0.8% and 19.4% (2011: 1.2%, 2021: 6.4%); opinions drift over time, so review age is a candidate feature and time is a limitation of a single 2021 snapshot.
